text:
The God who promises and the God who demands are never reconciled in Genesis 22. The narrator sets them side by side and does not choose between them. The reader is left where Abraham stands on the mountain, with the knife raised and the ram not yet seen, before a question which admits of no answer; and the want of an answer is the only answer given. Whoever reads the chapter is tried by it.

The story concerns reading more nearly than it concerns sacrifice. The weightiest matters in it are those the writer leaves unsaid. Abraham is silent; Isaac asks his question; Sarah is absent; the narrator offers no comment. Each of these is a gap, and each lays a demand upon the reader, whose burden grows heavier as the style grows sparer. What is withheld is what the reader receives: a father on Moriah, and a son who has asked.
